title: Self-Reconstructing Codazzi Defects, CP1 Quantization, and the Minimal Standard-Model Carrier
content: A current-residual reconstruction problem for a four-dimensional Lorentzian branch is analyzed. An Alena-Codazzi collar gives a local current-Codazzi closure on the punctured collar, and a penalty-dominant thin-core limit gives an integral-current core whose primitive regular component is read as a worldline defect with controlled boundary charge. Resolving the core gives a projective link $\mathbb{CP}^1$, while the primitive transverse class gives the line $\mathcal O(1)$. The positive Borel-Weil tower and the $\mathbb{CP}^1$ Toeplitz cutoff then turn a filtered transverse source into a finite internal support. After the scalar trace is separated, a transverse two-jet has only two non-scalar principal channels, the phase-current $V_1$ channel and the trace-free Codazzi-gap $V_2$ channel. In the Alena-Codazzi realization these channels are principal Codazzi-Gauss link charges, and their boundary superselection supplies the central separation. Toeplitz visibility then selects the rank-five carrier $E_3\oplus E_2$, with the degree-one class as the unique positive degree giving separated first thresholds. The split top-form condition and the local determinant-obstruction count have the same kernel, giving the compact carrier group $S(U(3)\times U(2))$. The determinant-compatible even exterior package gives the local one-generation Standard-Model module, while the determinant global form gives a $\mathbb Z_3$ family-response torsor. Exact family multiplicity, masses, mixing, CP, Majorana, and contact-class coefficients are treated as finite Schur-Kuranishi diagnostics of the completed Dirac-Callias/Riesz/Schur-Berry branch.
